topic: Useful and Harmful Changes in Materials
key_concepts: Cutting cloth, fabric, and wood into useful products is a useful material change.
Burning old tires, plastics, and garbage is harmful to the environment.
Dumping garbage on land pollutes soil and creates breeding places for pests.
Pests from polluted land carry germs that can cause diseases.
Polluted land cannot support plant growth.
Dumping garbage and chemical wastes into rivers pollutes water.
Drinking contaminated water can cause sickness.
Polluted water kills fish and water plants.
Smoke, ashes, and dust from factories and vehicles pollute air.
Polluted air can cause skin itchiness, lung infections, cancer, and respiratory diseases.
Deforestation causes soil erosion, habitat loss, and changes in air quality and rainfall.
Reforestation is planting trees to reduce harmful effects of deforestation.
